text:
Marathon Petroleum shares gained 1.15% today, continuing a sharp rally that has added nearly 9.3% over the past two weeks. The immediate driver is escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Iran launched missile and drone attacks on Kuwait and U.S. allies this week, pushing Brent crude above $96 per barrel and adding roughly 7% to oil prices just this week. Refineries are running at 98% capacity with tight inventory levels across gasoline and diesel, which amplifies the benefit of higher crude prices for a refiner like Marathon.

This move fits a broader pattern: as oil supply risks rise from regional conflict, refinery margins improve because refiners benefit from the spread between crude costs and fuel prices they can sell. With U.S. refineries already running near full capacity and storage inventories lean, tighter global supply pushes that spread wider.
